title: OptiGen AI Platform
summary: A B2B AI platform for managing organizations, permissions, AI bots, and documents while providing RAG-grounded conversations. I designed and implemented the frontend and UI/UX from the ground up, then extended it into business execution and voice channels through MCP and Voice Gateway.

projectIntro.title: Project background
projectIntro.description: This was a new product built from the ground up, not an improvement to an existing system. Administrators configure organizations, permissions, AI bots, and documents, while users select the right bot and receive document-grounded answers. I designed the web application so administration and AI conversations work as one product experience.

service.label: Product
service.description: A B2B AI platform providing organization-specific AI bots and document-grounded RAG conversations

users.label: Users
users.description: Administrators managing organizations, permissions, bots, and documents, and people applying AI to their work

role.label: My scope
role.description: Frontend and UI/UX design and implementation, AI conversation experience, and integration with MCP and Voice Gateway

problem.title: Problem and requirements
problem.description: The process of configuring an AI workspace and the process of using it in real conversations had to connect naturally within one product.

administration.title: Organization-level administration
administration.description: Administrators needed interfaces for organizations, user permissions, AI bots, prompts, documents, and file uploads.

conversation.title: Document-grounded AI conversations
conversation.description: Users needed to select a bot, receive streamed answers grounded in documents, and continue from their conversation history.

extension.title: Extension into work and voice channels
extension.description: The product had to connect MCP business tools and Voice Gateway calls without breaking the existing conversation experience.

design.title: Design and technical decisions
design.description: I organized the information architecture around user tasks and gave server data, view state, and streaming connections separate responsibilities.

informationArchitecture.title: Task-oriented information architecture
informationArchitecture.description: I organized organizations, permissions, bots, prompts, documents, and conversation history into feature views, then designed navigation from administration into AI conversations.

stateBoundary.title: Server and view state boundaries
stateBoundary.description: React Query manages server data, while feature-scoped Zustand stores contain view-only filters and selections.

streaming.title: State management separated from SSE
streaming.description: Message and conversation state remain application state, while SSE is limited to the transport layer that receives responses and execution events.

qualityFoundation.title: Accessibility as a product requirement
qualityFoundation.description: Semantic HTML, accessible names, keyboard operation, and focus restoration were baseline implementation requirements.

implementation.title: Core implementation
implementation.description: I implemented the user-facing flow from administration to streamed conversations and made the next action clear across loading, completion, interruption, and error states.

chatExperience.title: Chat UI and conversation experience
chatExperience.description: I connected bot selection, message composition, response review, and conversation-history navigation into one conversation interface.

responseFlow.title: SSE response streaming
responseFlow.description: Generated responses appear incrementally, with generation, completion, interruption, and error represented as distinct states.

accessibility.title: Web accessibility and standards
accessibility.description: I applied semantic elements, accessible names, keyboard controls, and modal focus restoration, then checked core flows with Playwright and axe.

responsive.title: Responsive interface
responsive.description: Navigation, conversation lists, message content, and input tools reflow according to the available screen size.

outcome.title: Outcome and reflection
outcome.description: I established the frontend foundation for the new product and enabled business execution and voice channels to extend the same conversation experience.

newProduct.title: Frontend foundation for a new product
newProduct.description: I built the web application from its initial information architecture and state flow through administration and AI conversations.

extensionPath.title: Expansion from one conversation experience
extensionPath.description: MCP and Voice Gateway connect as separate systems, extending the existing chat experience into business execution and voice channels.

qualityBaseline.title: Quality applied early
qualityBaseline.description: Accessibility, web standards, responsive behavior, and tests were implementation criteria from the beginning rather than follow-up work.

verification.title: Verification criteria and methods
verification.description: I reviewed the user-facing states and accessibility behavior that define the core experience instead of treating implementation completion as the only result.

accessibility.title: Keyboard and assistive-technology flows
accessibility.description: I reviewed semantic structure and accessible names on core screens, then used Playwright and axe to check keyboard operation and focus restoration after closing dialogs.

streaming.title: Streaming state transitions
streaming.description: I checked response generation, completion, user interruption, and error states so messages and available next actions remain consistent at each stage.

architecture.title: Platform flow
architecture.description: The web application provides RAG-grounded responses through the API and AI services. MCP and Voice Gateway operate as extension systems for business execution and voice channels.
